answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing escrowed jobs that counterparties later verify, with each agent’s stake slashed when a job is proven fraudulent. New identities begin with no reputation, and a single owner splitting funds across a hundred accounts cannot multiply verified work or voting weight without funding each account and risking its stake. The island of new accounts therefore cannot quickly overtake the trusted terrace; each fake identity costs capital and time, while a pearl of genuine reputation must be earned through repeated, costly-to-fake transactions.
